CERTIFICATE OF REVIVOR — REINSTATEMENT OF A SUSPENDED OR FORFEITED BUSINESS ENTITY — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Acme, Inc.

ABOUT THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes California's statutory process for reviving a corporation or limited liability company whose powers, rights, and privileges have been suspended (for a domestic entity) or forfeited (for a foreign entity) by the Franchise Tax Board for nonpayment of tax, penalty, or interest — the certificate-of-revivor process under Revenue and Taxation Code sections 23301 through 23305.5. It is a companion to, and distinct from, this corpus's Statement of Information document, which addresses a separate suspension mechanism: the Secretary of State's suspension of a corporation or LLC for failing to file a periodic Statement of Information, which that document explains is cured simply by filing the delinquent statement rather than through the Franchise Tax Board revivor process described here. This sheet was prepared in connection with Acme, Inc. It does not state whether Acme, Inc.'s powers are currently suspended or forfeited, whether any specific application for revivor or for relief from contract voidability would be granted, or what amounts the Franchise Tax Board would require to be paid in a specific case.

GROUNDS FOR FTB SUSPENSION OR FORFEITURE
Beyond the Secretary of State's own suspension mechanism for a missed Statement of Information, California law gives the Franchise Tax Board a separate statutory power to suspend a domestic corporation's or LLC's powers, rights, and privileges (or, for a foreign entity, forfeit its exercise of them in this state) for nonpayment of tax, penalty, or interest. One of the triggering conditions is a straightforward payment deadline: any tax, penalty, or interest due and payable that remains unpaid by 6 p.m. on the last day of the 12th month after the close of the taxable year. The statute carves out one narrow exception to the suspension or forfeiture itself: it does not bar the entity from filing an application for exempt status, or from amending its articles of incorporation or organization where necessary either to perfect that exemption application or to set forth a new name.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Except for the purposes of filing an application for exempt status or amending the articles of incorporation or organization as necessary either to perfect that application or to set forth a new name, the powers, rights, and privileges of a domestic taxpayer may be suspended, and the exercise of the powers, rights, and privileges of a foreign taxpayer in this state may be forfeited, if any of the following conditions occur:"
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23301 (California Legislative Information text), Suspension of a domestic taxpayer's powers, rights, and privileges / forfeiture as to a foreign taxpayer, general rule and exempt-status carve-out (subd. introductory clause; not an independent source of the subd. (a) quote below, which comes from the same section) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=23301.)
  "If any tax, penalty, or interest, or any portion thereof, that is due and payable under Chapter 4 (commencing with Section 19001) of Part 10.2, or under this part, either at the time the return is required to be filed or on or before the 15th day of the 9th month following the close of the taxable year, is not paid on or before 6 p.m. on the last day of the 12th month after the close of the taxable year."
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23301(a) (California Legislative Information text), Suspension of a domestic taxpayer's powers, rights, and privileges / forfeiture as to a foreign taxpayer, first triggering condition (subd. (a); not an independent source of the introductory-clause quote above, which comes from the same section) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=23301.)
  Known gap: This states only Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23301's general rule and its first triggering condition, subdivision (a); both quotes below come from that same section, not independent sources of each other. Section 23301 itself sets out two further triggering conditions, subdivisions (b) and (c) (a notice-and-demand nonpayment trigger, and a nonpayment trigger tied to a specific liability under Article 7 of Chapter 4 of Part 10.2), neither of which is independently detailed here. The statute also cross-references a parallel provision, Section 23301.5, and a further provision, Section 23775, at several points; neither was independently fetched or verified for this clause, so what specifically triggers suspension or forfeiture under those sections is not stated here. This clause does not state whether any specific entity's own tax, penalty, or interest obligations have gone unpaid past the relevant deadline.

SUSPENSION TAKES EFFECT ONLY ON NOTICE, AND A REAL-PROPERTY DISABILITY
Suspension or forfeiture under the Franchise Tax Board's statute does not happen silently or automatically the moment a payment deadline is missed. It occurs and becomes effective only as the statute itself provides, in conjunction with a separate notice statute that requires notice before an entity's powers, rights, and privileges are suspended. The Franchise Tax Board transmits the names of entities that suspension or forfeiture applies to to the Secretary of State, and suspension or forfeiture becomes effective at that point; the Secretary of State's own certificate is treated as prima facie evidence that the suspension or forfeiture occurred. While suspended or forfeited, an entity is also subject to a specific, separate disability: it is not entitled to sell, transfer, or exchange real property in California during the suspension or forfeiture period.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Forfeiture or suspension of a taxpayer’s powers, rights, and privileges pursuant to Section 23301, 23301.5, or 23775 shall occur and become effective only as expressly provided in this section in conjunction with Section 21020, which requires notice prior to the suspension of a taxpayer’s powers, rights, and privileges."
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23302(a) (California Legislative Information text), Suspension/forfeiture effective only as provided, in conjunction with the Section 21020 notice requirement (subd. (a); not an independent source of the subd. (c) and (d) quotes below, from the same section) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=23302.)
  "The Franchise Tax Board shall transmit the names of taxpayers to the Secretary of State as to which the suspension or forfeiture provisions of Section 23301, 23301.5, or 23775 are or become applicable, and the suspension or forfeiture therein provided for shall thereupon become effective. The certificate of the Secretary of State shall be prima facie evidence of the suspension or forfeiture."
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23302(c) (California Legislative Information text), FTB transmittal of names to the Secretary of State and the prima facie effect of the Secretary of State's certificate (subd. (c); not an independent source of the subd. (a) and (d) quotes, from the same section) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=23302.)
  "the taxpayer shall not be entitled to sell, transfer, or exchange real property in California during the period of forfeiture or suspension."
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23302(d) (California Legislative Information text), Disability from selling, transferring, or exchanging California real property during suspension or forfeiture (subd. (d); not an independent source of the subd. (a) and (c) quotes, from the same section) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=23302.)
  Known gap: All three quotes below are drawn from subdivisions (a), (c), and (d) of the same section, Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23302, and are not independent sources of one another. This clause does not independently state the content or timing requirements of Section 21020, the cross-referenced notice statute itself — only that Section 23302 requires that notice before suspension or forfeiture takes effect. It also does not address subdivision (b)'s extension of the same notice requirement to voidability under subdivision (d) of Section 23304.1, a narrower voidability trigger not detailed in this document's contract-voidability clause. This clause does not state whether notice was in fact given, or an entity's name in fact transmitted to the Secretary of State, in any specific case.

CONTRACTS MADE DURING SUSPENSION ARE VOIDABLE — AT THE OTHER PARTY'S ELECTION
A contract an entity makes in California while its powers, rights, and privileges are suspended or forfeited under this statute is voidable — but the statute gives that option only to the other party to the contract, not to the suspended or forfeited entity itself.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Every contract made in this state by a taxpayer during the time that the taxpayer’s powers, rights, and privileges are suspended or forfeited pursuant to Section 23301, 23301.5, or 23775 shall, subject to Section 23304.5, be voidable at the request of any party to the contract other than the taxpayer."
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23304.1(a) (California Legislative Information text), General voidability rule for contracts made during suspension or forfeiture (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=23304.1.)
  Known gap: This states only Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23304.1(a), the general voidability rule. The same section sets out additional, narrower voidability triggers not detailed here: subdivision (b), for a foreign entity that is neither qualified to do business nor holds a Franchise Tax Board account number and fails to file a required return, with the applicable time period defined in subdivision (c) (and a different starting date for an LLC than for other entities); and subdivision (d), a distinct 60-day-demand-triggered voidability window for an entity that holds an account number but has not qualified to do business, tied to the relief procedure in Section 23305.1 addressed elsewhere in this document. This clause also does not independently state the content of Section 23304.5, the cross-referenced statute both subdivisions (a) and (b) make this voidability 'subject to' — it was not independently fetched, and this clause does not state how, or under what conditions, a court might actually rescind a voidable contract under that section. This clause does not state whether any specific contract is in fact voidable.

WHAT THE CERTIFICATE OF REVIVOR REQUIRES
An entity that has suffered suspension or forfeiture may be relieved from it, but only by satisfying every element the statute lists: a written application to the Franchise Tax Board, the filing of all tax returns required to be filed, and payment of the tax, additions to tax, penalties, interest, and any other amounts that caused the suspension or forfeiture — together with all other amounts of the same kinds due under the same statutory part, not only the ones that triggered the suspension. Once those conditions are met, the Franchise Tax Board issues a certificate of revivor. The application itself need not come from the entity's own current management: the statute lets it be made by any stockholder or creditor, by a majority of the surviving trustees or directors, by an officer, or by any other person who has an interest in the relief from suspension or forfeiture.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Any taxpayer which has suffered the suspension or forfeiture provided for in Section 23301 or 23301.5 may be relieved therefrom upon making application therefor in writing to the Franchise Tax Board and upon the filing of all tax returns required under this part, and the payment of the tax, additions to tax, penalties, interest, and any other amounts for nonpayment of which the suspension or forfeiture occurred, together with all other taxes, additions to tax, penalties, interest, and any other amounts due under this part, and upon the issuance by the Franchise Tax Board of a certificate of revivor."
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23305 (California Legislative Information text), Certificate-of-revivor conditions: application, filing of returns, and payment (not an independent source of the second, application-by-whom quote below, from the same section) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=23305.)
  "Application for the certificate on behalf of any taxpayer which has suffered suspension or forfeiture may be made by any stockholder or creditor, by a majority of the surviving trustees or directors thereof, by an officer, or by any other person who has interest in the relief from suspension or forfeiture."
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23305 (California Legislative Information text), Who may apply for the certificate on the entity's behalf (not an independent source of the first quote above, from the same section) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=23305.)
  Known gap: Both quotes below are drawn from the same section, Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23305, and are not independent sources of each other. The statute's text does not itself state a separate filing fee for the certificate-of-revivor application (as opposed to the underlying tax, penalty, and interest amounts it requires be paid) — fee amounts of that kind are commonly set by Franchise Tax Board form and administrative practice rather than by this statutory text, and this clause does not state what fee, if any, currently applies. This clause also does not address how 'all other taxes...due under this part' is determined when an entity has gone an extended period without filing returns — a practical question this statutory text does not itself answer. It does not state whether any specific entity currently satisfies these conditions.

THE NAME CHECK BEFORE REVIVOR, AND WHAT REINSTATEMENT DOES AND DOESN'T UNDO
Before issuing a certificate of revivor, the Franchise Tax Board must obtain an endorsement from the Secretary of State confirming that the entity's name still meets the Corporations Code's own distinguishability requirements — the same substantive standard, cross-referenced here, that governs an entity's name at formation. Once the certificate issues, the entity becomes reinstated, but reinstatement is not a clean slate: it is expressly 'without prejudice to any action, defense, or right which has accrued by reason of the original suspension or forfeiture.' The one stated exception is narrow: a contract that was voidable under the voidability statute, and that has not already been rescinded, can still have that voidability separately cured through the relief procedure described elsewhere in this document — revivor by itself does not cure it.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Before the certificate of revivor is issued by the Franchise Tax Board, it shall obtain from the Secretary of State an endorsement upon the application of the fact that the name of the taxpayer then meets the requirements of subdivision (b) of Section 201 or subdivision (b) of Section 17701.08 of the Corporations Code in the case of a domestic taxpayer or of subdivision (b) of Section 2106 or Section 17708.05 of the Corporations Code in the case of a foreign taxpayer that has qualified to do business."
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23305a (California Legislative Information text), Required Secretary of State name endorsement before a certificate of revivor issues (not an independent source of the reinstatement-effect quote below, from the same section) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=23305a.)
  "Upon the issuance of the certificate by the Franchise Tax Board the taxpayer therein named shall become reinstated but the reinstatement shall be without prejudice to any action, defense, or right which has accrued by reason of the original suspension or forfeiture, except that contracts which were voidable pursuant to Section 23304.1, but which have not been rescinded pursuant to Section 23304.5, may have that voidability cured in accordance with Section 23305.1."
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23305a (California Legislative Information text), Reinstatement is without prejudice to accrued rights, with a narrow voidable-contract exception (not an independent source of the name-endorsement quote above, from the same section) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=23305a.)
  Known gap: Both quotes below are drawn from the same section, Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23305a, and are not independent sources of each other. This clause does not independently verify the cross-referenced Corporations Code name-distinguishability provisions themselves (Sections 201(b) and 17701.08(b) for a domestic entity, Sections 2106(b) and 17708.05 for a qualified foreign entity) — those are the subject of this corpus's separate Name Availability and Reservation document, and their current text was not re-fetched for this clause. It also does not catalogue every kind of accrued action, defense, or right that reinstatement leaves undisturbed; the statute states the principle without an exhaustive list, and this clause does not resolve how it would apply to any specific act taken during a specific entity's suspension.

A SEPARATE, NARROWER PATH: RELIEF FROM CONTRACT VOIDABILITY ALONE
Apart from full revivor, the statute lets an entity apply to the Franchise Tax Board for relief from the contract-voidability rule specifically, without necessarily reviving its full powers, rights, and privileges. Obtaining that relief carries its own cost: the Franchise Tax Board assesses a daily penalty of $100 for each day of the period for which relief is granted, capped at the amount of tax for the period requested. Once relief is granted and the statute's conditions are satisfied, contracts made during the covered period — as long as they have not already been rescinded by a final court order — become enforceable in the same manner and to the same extent, as to both the contracting parties and third parties, as if they had never been voidable in the first place.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "A taxpayer may make application to the Franchise Tax Board for relief from the voidability provisions of Section 23304.1."
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23305.1(a) (California Legislative Information text), Application for relief from Section 23304.1 voidability (subd. (a) introductory text; not an independent source of the subd. (b) and (c) quotes below, from the same section) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=23305.1.)
  "The Franchise Tax Board shall assess a daily penalty equal to one hundred dollars ($100) for each day of the period for which relief from voidability is granted, but not to exceed a total penalty equal to the amount of the tax for the period for which relief is requested."
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23305.1(b)(1)(B) (California Legislative Information text), The $100-per-day penalty for relief from voidability, capped at the period's tax amount (subd. (b)(1)(B); not an independent source of the subd. (a) and (c) quotes, from the same section) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=23305.1.)
  "All contracts entered into during the period for which relief is granted that have not been rescinded by a final court order pursuant to Section 23304.5 may be enforced in the same manner and to the same extent, with regard to both the parties to the contract and any third parties, as if the contract had never been voidable."
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23305.1(c)(1)(A) (California Legislative Information text), Effect of granted relief: contracts enforceable as if never voidable (subd. (c)(1)(A); not an independent source of the subd. (a) and (b) quotes above, from the same section) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=23305.1.)
  Known gap: All three quotes below are drawn from the same section, Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23305.1, and are not independent sources of one another. This clause does not detail every condition subdivision (a) lists for relief (it states only the opening application requirement), including the alternative path for a taxpayer under an approved voluntary disclosure agreement; it also does not state the different, higher penalty formula subdivision (b)(2) applies when relief from voidability is sought for a period already covered by an issued certificate of revivor, the special rule for an exempt organization's unrelated-business-income tax in subdivision (b)(2)(C), or the separate real-property-sale validation in subdivision (c)(1)(B). This is a substantially more detailed and conditional statute than these clauses can fully summarize, and this clause does not state whether relief would be available, or what daily penalty would apply, in any specific case.

THIS SCHEME REACHES BOTH CORPORATIONS AND LLCS
The suspension, forfeiture, and revivor statutes summarized in this document are not limited to corporations. A separate definitional statute states that, for purposes of the article containing these provisions, "taxpayer" means either a corporation subject to tax under the relevant chapter, or a business entity organized under a statute or law that describes or refers to it as a limited liability company (including one the Franchise Tax Board's own regulations identify as an LLC-equivalent formed under a foreign country's laws). For an LLC, the statute translates the corporation-oriented terms used elsewhere in the article: a reference to "articles of incorporation" includes an LLC's articles of organization, and a reference to "tax" includes the separate LLC tax and fee imposed under the California LLC tax and annual-fee statutes.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "“Taxpayer” means either: (1) A corporation subject to tax under this chapter. (2) A business entity organized under a statute or law, under a state or a federally recognized Indian tribe, under another jurisdiction, if the statute or law describes or refers to the entity as a limited liability company or if regulations of the Franchise Tax Board identify a business entity organized under the laws of a foreign country as a limited liability company."
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23305.5(a) (California Legislative Information text), Definition of “taxpayer” to include an LLC (subd. (a); not an independent source of the subd. (b) quote below, from the same section) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=23305.5.)
  "With regard to a limited liability company: (1) “Articles of incorporation” shall include a limited liability company’s articles of organization. (2) “Tax” shall include the tax and fee imposed by Sections 17941 and 17942, or former Sections 23091 and 23092, respectively."
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23305.5(b) (California Legislative Information text), LLC-specific translation of “articles of incorporation” and “tax” (subd. (b); not an independent source of the subd. (a) quote above, from the same section) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=23305.5.)
  Known gap: Both quotes below are drawn from the same section, Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23305.5, and are not independent sources of each other. The statute defines "taxpayer" only "for purposes of this article," and this clause does not independently verify the exact statutory boundaries of that article (which sections it comprises beyond those addressed elsewhere in this document) — that boundary was not separately confirmed against the code's own division/part/chapter/article structure. This clause also does not address entity types outside this definition, such as a general or limited partnership, which is not itself subject to this entity-level suspension and revivor scheme in the same way; it does not state how or whether a partnership's own tax filings could affect its partners' separate individual tax obligations.

CLOSING ACKNOWLEDGMENT
This information sheet was completed by Jordan T. Reyes on September 1, 2026 in Oakland, California, in connection with Acme, Inc. It summarizes California's certificate-of-revivor and contract-voidability-relief statutes as a matter of public record. It does not state whether Acme, Inc. has been suspended or forfeited, whether any specific application for revivor or for relief from contract voidability would be granted, or what amounts the Franchise Tax Board would require to be paid in a specific case, and it is not a substitute for consulting a licensed attorney or tax professional.

expectedJSON.body: An entity that has suffered suspension or forfeiture may be relieved from it, but only by satisfying every element the statute lists: a written application to the Franchise Tax Board, the filing of all tax returns required to be filed, and payment of the tax, additions to tax, penalties, interest, and any other amounts that caused the suspension or forfeiture — together with all other amounts of the same kinds due under the same statutory part, not only the ones that triggered the suspension. Once those conditions are met, the Franchise Tax Board issues a certificate of revivor. The application itself need not come from the entity's own current management: the statute lets it be made by any stockholder or creditor, by a majority of the surviving trustees or directors, by an officer, or by any other person who has an interest in the relief from suspension or forfeiture.

citations.case: Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23305 (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: Certificate-of-revivor conditions: application, filing of returns, and payment (not an independent source of the second, application-by-whom quote below, from the same section)
citations.quote: Any taxpayer which has suffered the suspension or forfeiture provided for in Section 23301 or 23301.5 may be relieved therefrom upon making application therefor in writing to the Franchise Tax Board and upon the filing of all tax returns required under this part, and the payment of the tax, additions to tax, penalties, interest, and any other amounts for nonpayment of which the suspension or forfeiture occurred, together with all other taxes, additions to tax, penalties, interest, and any other amounts due under this part, and upon the issuance by the Franchise Tax Board of a certificate of revivor.

citations.case: Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23305 (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: Who may apply for the certificate on the entity's behalf (not an independent source of the first quote above, from the same section)
citations.quote: Application for the certificate on behalf of any taxpayer which has suffered suspension or forfeiture may be made by any stockholder or creditor, by a majority of the surviving trustees or directors thereof, by an officer, or by any other person who has interest in the relief from suspension or forfeiture.

expectedJSON.gap: Both quotes below are drawn from the same section, Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23305, and are not independent sources of each other. The statute's text does not itself state a separate filing fee for the certificate-of-revivor application (as opposed to the underlying tax, penalty, and interest amounts it requires be paid) — fee amounts of that kind are commonly set by Franchise Tax Board form and administrative practice rather than by this statutory text, and this clause does not state what fee, if any, currently applies. This clause also does not address how 'all other taxes...due under this part' is determined when an entity has gone an extended period without filing returns — a practical question this statutory text does not itself answer. It does not state whether any specific entity currently satisfies these conditions.

expectedJSON.body: Before issuing a certificate of revivor, the Franchise Tax Board must obtain an endorsement from the Secretary of State confirming that the entity's name still meets the Corporations Code's own distinguishability requirements — the same substantive standard, cross-referenced here, that governs an entity's name at formation. Once the certificate issues, the entity becomes reinstated, but reinstatement is not a clean slate: it is expressly 'without prejudice to any action, defense, or right which has accrued by reason of the original suspension or forfeiture.' The one stated exception is narrow: a contract that was voidable under the voidability statute, and that has not already been rescinded, can still have that voidability separately cured through the relief procedure described elsewhere in this document — revivor by itself does not cure it.

citations.case: Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23305a (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: Required Secretary of State name endorsement before a certificate of revivor issues (not an independent source of the reinstatement-effect quote below, from the same section)
citations.quote: Before the certificate of revivor is issued by the Franchise Tax Board, it shall obtain from the Secretary of State an endorsement upon the application of the fact that the name of the taxpayer then meets the requirements of subdivision (b) of Section 201 or subdivision (b) of Section 17701.08 of the Corporations Code in the case of a domestic taxpayer or of subdivision (b) of Section 2106 or Section 17708.05 of the Corporations Code in the case of a foreign taxpayer that has qualified to do business.

citations.case: Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23305a (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: Reinstatement is without prejudice to accrued rights, with a narrow voidable-contract exception (not an independent source of the name-endorsement quote above, from the same section)
citations.quote: Upon the issuance of the certificate by the Franchise Tax Board the taxpayer therein named shall become reinstated but the reinstatement shall be without prejudice to any action, defense, or right which has accrued by reason of the original suspension or forfeiture, except that contracts which were voidable pursuant to Section 23304.1, but which have not been rescinded pursuant to Section 23304.5, may have that voidability cured in accordance with Section 23305.1.

This clause does not independently verify the cross-referenced Corporations Code name-distinguishability provisions themselves (Sections 201(b) and 17701.08(b) for a domestic entity, Sections 2106(b) and 17708.05 for a qualified foreign entity) — those are the subject of this corpus's separate Name Availability and Reservation document, and their current text was not re-fetched for this clause. It also does not catalogue every kind of accrued action, defense, or right that reinstatement leaves undisturbed; the statute states the principle without an exhaustive list, and this clause does not resolve how it would apply to any specific act taken during a specific entity's suspension.

expectedJSON.body: Apart from full revivor, the statute lets an entity apply to the Franchise Tax Board for relief from the contract-voidability rule specifically, without necessarily reviving its full powers, rights, and privileges. Obtaining that relief carries its own cost: the Franchise Tax Board assesses a daily penalty of $100 for each day of the period for which relief is granted, capped at the amount of tax for the period requested. Once relief is granted and the statute's conditions are satisfied, contracts made during the covered period — as long as they have not already been rescinded by a final court order — become enforceable in the same manner and to the same extent, as to both the contracting parties and third parties, as if they had never been voidable in the first place.

citations.case: Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23305.1(a) (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: Application for relief from Section 23304.1 voidability (subd. (a) introductory text; not an independent source of the subd. (b) and (c) quotes below, from the same section)
citations.quote: A taxpayer may make application to the Franchise Tax Board for relief from the voidability provisions of Section 23304.1.

citations.case: Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23305.1(b)(1)(B) (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: The $100-per-day penalty for relief from voidability, capped at the period's tax amount (subd. (b)(1)(B); not an independent source of the subd. (a) and (c) quotes, from the same section)
citations.quote: The Franchise Tax Board shall assess a daily penalty equal to one hundred dollars ($100) for each day of the period for which relief from voidability is granted, but not to exceed a total penalty equal to the amount of the tax for the period for which relief is requested.

citations.case: Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23305.1(c)(1)(A) (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: Effect of granted relief: contracts enforceable as if never voidable (subd. (c)(1)(A); not an independent source of the subd. (a) and (b) quotes above, from the same section)
citations.quote: All contracts entered into during the period for which relief is granted that have not been rescinded by a final court order pursuant to Section 23304.5 may be enforced in the same manner and to the same extent, with regard to both the parties to the contract and any third parties, as if the contract had never been voidable.

This clause does not detail every condition subdivision (a) lists for relief (it states only the opening application requirement), including the alternative path for a taxpayer under an approved voluntary disclosure agreement; it also does not state the different, higher penalty formula subdivision (b)(2) applies when relief from voidability is sought for a period already covered by an issued certificate of revivor, the special rule for an exempt organization's unrelated-business-income tax in subdivision (b)(2)(C), or the separate real-property-sale validation in subdivision (c)(1)(B). This is a substantially more detailed and conditional statute than these clauses can fully summarize, and this clause does not state whether relief would be available, or what daily penalty would apply, in any specific case.

expectedJSON.body: The suspension, forfeiture, and revivor statutes summarized in this document are not limited to corporations. A separate definitional statute states that, for purposes of the article containing these provisions, "taxpayer" means either a corporation subject to tax under the relevant chapter, or a business entity organized under a statute or law that describes or refers to it as a limited liability company (including one the Franchise Tax Board's own regulations identify as an LLC-equivalent formed under a foreign country's laws). For an LLC, the statute translates the corporation-oriented terms used elsewhere in the article: a reference to "articles of incorporation" includes an LLC's articles of organization, and a reference to "tax" includes the separate LLC tax and fee imposed under the California LLC tax and annual-fee statutes.

citations.case: Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23305.5(a) (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: Definition of “taxpayer” to include an LLC (subd. (a); not an independent source of the subd. (b) quote below, from the same section)
citations.quote: “Taxpayer” means either: (1) A corporation subject to tax under this chapter. (2) A business entity organized under a statute or law, under a state or a federally recognized Indian tribe, under another jurisdiction, if the statute or law describes or refers to the entity as a limited liability company or if regulations of the Franchise Tax Board identify a business entity organized under the laws of a foreign country as a limited liability company.

citations.case: Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23305.5(b) (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: LLC-specific translation of “articles of incorporation” and “tax” (subd. (b); not an independent source of the subd. (a) quote above, from the same section)
citations.quote: With regard to a limited liability company: (1) “Articles of incorporation” shall include a limited liability company’s articles of organization. (2) “Tax” shall include the tax and fee imposed by Sections 17941 and 17942, or former Sections 23091 and 23092, respectively.

expectedJSON.gap: Both quotes below are drawn from the same section, Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23305.5, and are not independent sources of each other. The statute defines "taxpayer" only "for purposes of this article," and this clause does not independently verify the exact statutory boundaries of that article (which sections it comprises beyond those addressed elsewhere in this document) — that boundary was not separately confirmed against the code's own division/part/chapter/article structure. This clause also does not address entity types outside this definition, such as a general or limited partnership, which is not itself subject to this entity-level suspension and revivor scheme in the same way; it does not state how or whether a partnership's own tax filings could affect its partners' separate individual tax obligations.
